plain_english: Since intellect's arising, actual or not, stands unperceived by any spirit — puruṣārthatā in such a case [is unspeakable: v38].
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ syādasya buddhestu saṃbhavannapyasaṃbhavī vinā saṃvedyatāṃ puṃsastathātve puruṣārthatā

plain_english: Even of spirit, even of pradhāna, it would be unspeakable — of the mere; yet mind's function, or intellect's, is individually conditioned.
sanskrit_cite: puṃso'pi syātpradhānasyāvācyā sā kevalasya tu athāpi manaso vṛttirbuddhervaikaikasaṃskṛtā

plain_english: Will, indeed — how could it serve all spirits' purposes? But [if] it belongs to generic pradhāna, for all…
sanskrit_cite: icchā nāma kathaṃ sarvapuruṣārthopayoginī syātikiṃ tu sā pradhānasya sāmānyasyākhilānprati

plain_english: Even unperceived by spirit, could it be? Not will — and perceived, by whom would it be? If by all — omniscience of each and every one follows.
sanskrit_cite: puṃsaḥ syātsāpyasaṃvedyā necchā vedyā ca kasya sā sarveṣāṃ yadi sārvajñyamekaikasya prasajyate

plain_english: Through light-unity the distinct appearances would mix; yet [perceived] by some one undivided from all spirits…
Not from world-sustenance-purpose would it produce seed into sprout; but by nature — such a kit is its cause, of such a kind.
sanskrit_cite: na lokayātrābhiprāyājjanayedbījamaṅkuram kiṃ tu svabhāvātsā tasya sāmagrī heturīdṛśaḥ

plain_english: What is born, fit — the wise man joins to one another; by this courtesy, puruṣārthatva is spoken of it.
sanskrit_cite: yajjātaṃ yogyamanyonyaṃ yojayedbuddhimāñjanaḥ asya tenopacāreṇa puruṣārthatvamucyate

plain_english: If thus — even on completion, even in purpose, toward him [the freed spirit]…
From own-effect-change the root-cause would not cease; oh — it does not cease, this beyond, in the seven of nature.
sanskrit_cite: svakāryapariṇāmānna viramenmūlakāraṇam āho na viramatyetatparaṃ prakṛtisaptake
